name: Bigthan
overview: Bigthan was a male figure known for his involvement in a plot against King Ahasuerus, as recorded in the Book of Esther. Beyond this notable act, Scripture provides limited information about his background or tribal affiliation. His role highlights the presence of opposition within the king's court during Esther's time.
namesAndTitles: The name Bigthan, also appearing as Bigthana, means 'gift of God.' This proper name reflects a common theophoric element in biblical names, though it was not given by God directly. Both forms of the name appear in the Book of Esther, underscoring the same individual involved in the narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Bigthan beyond his involvement in the plot against King Ahasuerus. There are no known relatives or connections listed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Bigthan's significance lies in his role as a conspirator against King Ahasuerus, which reveals the internal threats faced by the Persian monarchy during Esther's story. His attempted treason is part of the broader narrative demonstrating God's providential protection over the king and the unfolding of His plan for His people. Though a minor character, Bigthan's actions contribute to the tension and eventual deliverance found in the Book of Esther.
